chapter: Swing, singers, Ed Fox and recordings
title: Ed Fox as manager and paymaster
summary: Fox signed Hines to a long contract and paid all; lawsuit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Guess Earl does have a knack for -- what was Ed Fox's role in all of this? You know, the changes, and the shows, and then later he and Earl got in a big falling out.
Yeah. Well, Ed Fox's main role was manager and owner of Earl.
Owner of Earl?
Yeah.
Earl had something like a 20-year contract.

Earl kind of messed up there, one while there in the early years he signed a ten-year contract with Ed Fox, but Ed Fox didn't manage him. Ed Fox collected all the money, paid him off, and everything. Where he paid George Dixon the money for the sidemen. He paid Earl separate.

So finally Earl began -- after a few years he began to wake up, after the band got to be real popular and real good, he began to wake up, and he wanted to break away from his contract. That's when the falling out come in.
There was a lawsuit, I believe.
Yeah.
That was about 1940.
Yeah.
Well, in other words, Earl didn't pay the band?
No.
Fox paid the band?
Fox paid the band.
And if you wanted a raise, you dealt with Fox?
Yeah, which you didn't ask for raises back in them days.
But if you did, you would have to deal with him?
You'd have to deal with him.
If somebody left, who'd they quit to?
You'd give Earl the notice. He's the bandleader.
That's what I'm trying to get at. Who was running what?

Yeah. Earl was the bandleader, you gave your notice to Earl. Most of the time when Earl was off the bandstand, George Dixon directed the band. He paid the band off, like on rules, and one-nighters. The road
manager gave the money to George Dixon, George Dixon would pay the band. He'd give Earl his money separately.
Did everybody get the same amount of money?
Yeah, everybody got the same amount.
And then you mentioned last week that toward the end -- that money started getting shorter and shorter.
Band started falling off at the Grand Terrace, and that's the way Ed Fox paid off.
Well, if you did a lot of business did you get more money?
We didn't do a lot of business. When it started falling off, it really started going down.
But I mean before that, when you'd do a lot of business, you had a better week one week than another --
Same amount of money. Cause you're making a salary.
Then when it fell off, then you got less money?
Yeah, you got less money. You know, it'd be short.
